title: A Point Sliding Along an Arc
statement: Two circles of equal radius have centres $A$ and $B$. The circle centred at $A$ passes through $B$, and the circle centred at $B$ passes through $A$. Let $E$ be one of the two points where the circles intersect. The line $AB$ meets the circle centred at $A$ at $B$ and at a second point $C$. A point $P$ moves along the arc $CE$ of the circle centred at $A$ that does not contain $B$, and $P$ is never equal to $C$ or $E$. How many different integer values can the degree measure of $\angle BEP$ take?
hints: Draw the radii $AE$ and $AP$. What kind of triangle is $ABE$, and what kind is $AEP$?

Use angle chasing. Triangle $ABE$ has three sides equal to the common radius, and triangle $AEP$ is isosceles because $AE = AP$. Split $\angle BEP$ along the ray $EA$ into $\angle BEA$ and $\angle AEP$.

Let $\theta = \angle EAP$. Then $\theta$ can be any value strictly between $0^\circ$ and $120^\circ$, and $\angle AEP = 90^\circ - \frac{\theta}{2}$. Adding $\angle BEA = 60^\circ$ shows that $\angle BEP$ takes every value strictly between $90^\circ$ and $150^\circ$. Now count the integers in this range.
solution:
Triangle $ABE$ is equilateral, so $\angle BEA=\angle BAE=60^\circ$ and $\angle EAC=120^\circ$. Hence $\theta=\angle EAP$ takes every value in $(0^\circ,120^\circ)$.

Since $AE=AP$, $\angle AEP=90^\circ-\frac{\theta}{2}$.

Points $B$ and $C$ lie on opposite sides of line $AE$, and the arc $EC$ (central angle less than $180^\circ$) lies on $C$'s side, so $P$ and $B$ are on opposite sides of $AE$. As $60^\circ+90^\circ-\frac{\theta}{2}<180^\circ$, ray $EA$ lies inside $\angle BEP$, so
$$\angle BEP=60^\circ+90^\circ-\dfrac{\theta}{2}=150^\circ-\dfrac{\theta}{2},$$
which takes every value in $(90^\circ,150^\circ)$. The integers are $91,\dots,149$, giving $59$ values.

solution_figures.alt: Two equal circles with centres A and B, each passing through the other's centre, meet at E. C is the second point where line AB meets the circle centred at A, and P lies on arc CE away from B. Triangle ABE is equilateral with a 60 degree angle at E, triangle AEP is isosceles with AE = AP and apex angle theta at A, and segment EP is highlighted.
